messages.speaker: Professor Chen
messages.text: Soldier, we will begin with your judgment after Operation Mirador. Some answers reveal more than they say.

messages.speaker: Professor Chen
messages.text: Trauma can shift judgment without erasing memory. I need to know whether you still decide from the present.

choices.label: Give me a clear frame and I will answer precisely.
Before that, I want to know what happened to my unit.
If this is an interrogation, I keep control of my answers.

messages.speaker: Professor Chen
messages.text: Imagine the scene. The radio orders you to secure the egg. At the same time, a wounded teammate calls from the contaminated corridor.

choices.label: I lock down the egg first. The order protects the greatest number.
I pull out the wounded soldier. No protocol is worth an abandoned life.
I observe the egg before acting: if it reacts to the scene, it may reveal a way out.

messages.speaker: Professor Chen
messages.text: The egg's pulsatic cardiograph... accelerates during your answer... My theory is being confirmed... If you had to transmit one moral value to this creature, which would you choose?

choices.label: Strength: protect first, strike if the threat comes closer.
Lucidity: understand before deciding who the enemy is.
Compassion: preserve a life while it can still be preserved.
